background: Nationwide Building Society is the largest building society in the world and the UK's second-largest mortgage lender, a mutual funded by retail savings and current accounts and lending mainly on residential mortgages, now also the owner of Virgin Money.
synthesis: The society is rated A+ on average across all three main agencies, all three on a stable outlook, with the last move a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026, the highest grades of any UK building society. Capital is mixed against UK building societies: CET1 of 18.6% is above the peer median, but leverage of 5.2% is in the bottom quarter. Liquidity is also mixed, with LCR of 174% below the peer median and NSFR of 145% at the median. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods. The newest flagged item, on 2 Jul 2026, is job cuts following the Virgin Money takeover, a cost measure rather than a credit event.
